quote.text: At dawn, when you have trouble getting out of bed, tell yourself: “I have to go to work — as a human being. What do I have to complain of, if I’m going to do what I was born for — the things I was brought into the world to do? Or is this what I was created for? To huddle under the blankets and stay warm?” So you were born to feel “nice”? Instead of doing things and experiencing them? Don’t you see the plants, the birds, the ants and spiders and bees going about their individual tasks, putting the world in order, as best they can? And you’re not willing to do your job as a human being? Why aren’t you running to do what your nature demands? You don’t love yourself enough. Or you’d love your nature too, and what it demands of you.
quote.author: Marcus Aurelius
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood:
    • Recognize that each new day is a call to nurture and guide your children, much like nature compels every creature to fulfill its role; rising early and engaging fully sets an example of commitment and resilience.
    • View the challenges of parenthood as opportunities to instill discipline and self-love in your children, reminding them that growth comes from embracing life’s demands rather than seeking comfort in inertia.
  • Leadership:
    • Understand that true leadership means rising to your responsibilities with vigor, much like the natural world that never hesitates to fulfill its purpose; your actions inspire those you guide.
    • By approaching challenges with the same earnest energy as the birds, the ants, and the bees, you create an environment where duty and purpose drive collective progress and unity.
  • Product Management:
    • Embrace your role as a product manager by recognizing each project as part of a larger natural order—a deliberate, meaningful contribution that evolves and improves with time.
    • Just as nature thrives on continuous effort and adaptation, your commitment to refining processes and meeting user needs not only drives innovation but also reflects the essence of purposeful existence.
